evidence.exact_quote:
**Editor result is mode-dependent and can partially commit.** [external.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/v0.44.0/cli/src/merge_tools/external.rs) (`S00025`, 72–91, 198–220, 271–330) distinguishes tools whose output is accepted as a full resolution from tools configured to edit markers. For the latter, or configured conflict exit codes, it reparses output with the original terms and expected length. Other nonzero exits abort; empty/unchanged output is rejected; a conflict exit with no valid remaining conflict is rejected. Tool-specific marker-style overrides and `$marker_length` affect the path. It is incorrect to claim every successful editor invocation reparses markers automatically.

For multiple files, `external.rs` 343–380 can return a partially changed tree together with a later error. [resolve.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/v0.44.0/cli/src/commands/resolve.rs) (`S00015`, 112–147) writes that tree and finishes the transaction **before returning the partial-resolution error**. The test `test_multiple_conflicts_with_error` (`S00029`, 2077–2125) expects file1's resolution saved, file2 still conflicted and exit 1. Direct text editing requires a subsequent native snapshot; `jj resolve` itself reads temporary editor output and records a rewritten commit. Treat these as distinct paths when verifying post-editor state.

**Native inspection data and remaining gaps.** `jj resolve --list` enumerates native conflicted paths but has no template argument in `ResolveArgs`, and no-conflict/no-matching-path results are errors (`S00015`, 50–105). [print_conflicted_paths](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/v0.44.0/cli/src/cli_util.rs) (`S00035`, 3070–3158) simplifies terms and prints path, side count and special/deleted object categories; a backend error propagates. A listing failure is not proof of resolution. [Templates](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/v0.44.0/docs/templates.md) (`S00020`, 290–298, 788–800) offer `commit.conflict()`, `conflicted_files()`, path, file type and side count through `TreeEntry`. These support native enumeration, but the inspected `TreeEntry` API does not expose the complete original term/object identity and is not directly serializable. Explicitly map its fields; preserve exact commit/repository/path context and use deeper native data where term identity is required. JSON schema stability has the caveat recorded under L-28f7a36f8557.

**Logical model and representations.** [v0.44.0 conflicts documentation](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/v0.44.0/docs/conflicts.md) (local `research-evidence/sources/S00026/text.txt`, lines 11–18) says rebase can succeed with a conflict recorded in the commit, and “what's stored in the commit is a logical representation of the conflict, not conflict markers.” This does not assert that every rebase succeeds despite unrelated errors. The same file is byte-identical as fetched text to the handoff revision (`S00004`). Its passages establish arbitrarily many sides (109–113), diff/snapshot/Git-diff3 styles (93–97, 121–167), Git fallback to snapshot for more than two sides (165–167), collision-avoiding longer markers (169–187), and missing-final-newline encoding (190–219): add a separator newline to each term and omit the newline on the closing marker.

[v0.44.0 technical conflicts](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/v0.44.0/docs/technical/conflicts.md) (`S00027`, 15–39, 44–57) describes an ordered odd-length tree merge such as `A+(C-B)+(E-D)` and cancellation of terms on subsequent rebases. “Three-way” means two sides and a base, not three sides. The same document (65–74) warns that the default same-change rule is algebraically lossy; do not expand logical conflict support into a universal guarantee of lossless rebase roundtrips.

[v0.44.0 conflicts.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/v0.44.0/lib/src/conflicts.rs) (`S00007`, 394–430) accepts marker-like runs followed by whitespace/end and parses markers of **at least** the expected length, ignoring shorter ones. Length is chosen above marker-like lines already present. The materializer's style dispatch and newline handling are at 516–564. Thus seven fixed ASCII characters are not a complete parser, and marker recognition depends on the original conflict's expected length and side count.

**Snapshot and partial-term preservation.** [Working-copy docs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/v0.44.0/docs/working-copy.md) (`S00014`, 9–12, 31–58) say most commands snapshot changed files, reparsing conflict markers, and allow resolving part of a conflict by editing its terms. `update_from_content` (`S00007`, 1047–1125) simplifies original file-ID terms, parses using the simplified side count, returns the original terms when hunks are unchanged, writes changed terms and expands back to the original arity when needed. It returns a normal file if **no valid markers of the expected arity** remain (1081–1084), including malformed-marker cases. Native resolution state can therefore treat marker-looking text as ordinary file content; a visual marker scan is not a substitute for querying native state, and native clean state alone does not prove the user intended every byte.

The [v0.44.0 library test source](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/v0.44.0/lib/tests/test_conflicts.rs) (`S00028`, 1755–1804 and 1854–1943) asserts unchanged term identity, changed IDs after partial resolution, and preservation of unsimplified terms. The malformed-input test (2364 onward) includes invalid marker text inside a still-conflicted result. Tests were read, not executed.

**Trailing-CR discrepancy resolved against code.**

- [Issue #9868](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/issues/9868), retrieved through the [primary API](https://api.github.com/repos/jj-vcs/jj/issues/9868) (`S00017`), reports jj-lib **0.43.0**, Git markers, terms `left\r`, `base`, `right`, and loss of the CR after materialize/parse. The API response still says `state: open`; this is issue metadata, not release evidence. Its prose calls `left\r` “three bytes,” which is a typo: the illustrated input contains five bytes.
- v0.44.0 `parse_conflict` (`S00007`, 838–875) removes the added LF and then removes any final CR **without checking the separator's EOL style**. The materializer's EOL detector (433–446) uses LF when the terms have no LF. Hence a content CR can be mistaken for a separator CR. This independently verifies applicability to 0.44.0 rather than merely extrapolating from the 0.43 issue.
- [Fix commit f1d7a873e3e04fae0765c3adaaa152fb55a00931](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/commit/f1d7a873e3e04fae0765c3adaaa152fb55a00931), [patch](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/commit/f1d7a873e3e04fae0765c3adaaa152fb55a00931.patch) (`S00016`, 7–34, 61–127), records whether the opening marker ended with CRLF and removes CR only then. The commit explains that the missing byte otherwise compares as a real edit during `update_from_content` and gets written on snapshot. [Commit metadata](https://api.github.com/repos/jj-vcs/jj/commits/f1d7a873e3e04fae0765c3adaaa152fb55a00931) (`S00030`) distinguishes author date **2026-07-29** from committer date **2026-08-07**; the handoff's August 7 is supported as the latter.

The [changelog](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/CHANGELOG.md) (`S00009`, 69, 124–127) assigns the fix to **0.45.0, September 2, 2026**. This closes the old “fix unfound/exact-0.44 comparison pending” prose; the retained follow-up is supported by independent fetches.
- The added regression test (`S00031`, 1417–1443) covers LF and actual CRLF separators, each with content ending in bare CR, using **Git style, line-level merging, `SameChange::Keep`**. It does not alone prove every style, mixed-EOL editor, binary input or working-copy runtime path. Simply stopping all CR removal would break the CRLF-separator case; the conditional fix is substantive. No test was run here.

That absolute statement is too strong for this version: the file-versus-directory test (`S00029`, 926–966) expects an error listing removing/adding file/tree object IDs **and commit/change labels**. claims.proposition: Track clone setup, fetch, preset writing, checkout and residual-directory cleanup with exact destination identity; protect existing and dirty directories.
claims.mapping_rationale: Clone phase/residual cleanup and destination identity distinctions.

evidence.exact_quote:
- Admission: lines 175–191 reject `--at-op` with “--at-op is not respected” before creating the destination, record `wc_path.exists()`, and reject an existing nonempty directory. Tests 126–176 and 363–386 explicitly check preservation of existing empty destinations and existing repositories; the latter are rejected before clone starts. This is not evidence about concurrent replacement after admission.
- **Earlier uncovered boundary:** lines 194–220 call `create_dir_all` before fallible colocation configuration, branch/tag pattern parsing, object-hash configuration and canonicalization. These `?` returns precede `clone_result`, so an error there can leave created directories. The guarded cleanup also removes only the destination itself, not newly created ancestor directories. These are control-flow deductions, not executed reproductions.
- Guarded stage: lines 222–260 cover workspace initialization, remote configuration, fetch/import and associated transaction completion. On error, lines 261–285 *attempt* `.jj` deletion, then `.git` deletion when colocated, then `remove_dir` on the root only if the original existence check said it was new. `NotFound` is ignored for metadata directories. Any other deletion error short-circuits the closure, so cleanup can stop before remaining paths; warning output is best-effort and the original clone error is returned. Replace any implication of guaranteed cleanup with this narrower statement.
- Later stage: lines 287–322 propagate preset-write, checkout and transaction-finish errors outside that guard. Checkout is conditional on a selected branch with a normal remote target; an empty remote or unmatched branch selection may validly have no selected branch. Even the commit lookup is `if let Ok(commit)`, not an unconditional checkout guarantee. Lines 350–365 and 391–459 show separate remote-configuration/fetch transactions; this is not one atomic clone operation.
- The source test `test_git_clone_malformed`, lines 1084–1135, expects a `.jj` path in the remote tree to cause **checkout failure after fetch and preset messages**, then expects `status` to report a retained stale working copy. Its first `workspace update-stale` attempt fails again; the test recovers by selecting `root()` with `--ignore-working-copy`. This directly supports the later failure boundary; it does not establish a universal recovery recipe.
- Success also depends on requested mode: `test_git_clone_ignore_working_copy`, lines 785–820, expects clone success without updating working-copy files and a later ordinary status to report staleness. A zero exit in this mode is not evidence of populated files. `test_git_clone_at_operation`, lines 824–837, expects exit 2 for `--at-op`.
- Colocation is default unless config/flags alter it (source 77–105, 198–202); `--no-colocate` and `--colocate` are mutually exclusive. Depth, ref selection and object hash are explicit source options (107–159). A review must record the effective mode, not infer it from a version number.

**Version reconciliation.** Fetched normalized source text at handoff revision `e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215` (`S00003`) and v0.44.0 (`S00006`) is byte-identical, SHA-256 `505b6c62e85fb6bcb50d3d816fad583a020651e8a7860b50932fb849c6f54136`. This independently confirms the retained follow-up and closes the older exact-file comparison deferral. It proves equivalence of this command file only, not all dependencies or environments.

**Supported lesson and alternatives.** Preserve separate observations for destination creation, initialization, fetch/import completion, preset persistence, repository transaction completion, working-copy materialization and cleanup outcome. A retained fetched repository can support explicit recovery; deletion/retry is not the only outcome. The v0.44.0 [working-copy documentation](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/v0.44.0/docs/working-copy.md#stale-working-copy) (`S00014`, lines 94–118) distinguishes recorded operations from working-copy updates and identifies interruption as a possible cause of staleness.

**Unresolved.** The inspected code is an explicit error branch, not proof that a killed/cancelled process reaches cleanup. Authentication cancellation, subprocess shutdown, preset-write interruption, partial checkout and cleanup failure need fault-injection evidence in a separately authorized executable study. Canonicalizing a path and remembering a Boolean do not establish persistent directory identity; replacement/symlink races and concurrent new contents remain unverified hypotheses, not demonstrated data-loss bugs. Preserve destination identity, residual-directory disposition and caller continuation as investigation directions; native source does not establish a caller-navigation contract. Tests above were read, not run.

evidence.exact_quote:
**Exact API/version reconciliation.** Comparison of v0.44.0 (`S00005`) with handoff revision `e9f48b3…` (`S00002`) found only a wording change to the `--no-graph` help comment. The substantive command code matches. v0.44.0 [templates](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/v0.44.0/docs/templates.md) (`S00020`, 250–313) expose commit/change IDs, divergence, hidden state, `CommitEvolutionEntry.commit`, `operation`, `predecessors`, and normalized `inter_diff`. Release history (`S00009`, 2187–2188) dates operation-backed evolution to **0.30.0**. It puts multi-start evolog in **0.31.0** (2047–2048), the `CommitEvolutionEntry`/`templates.evolog` transition in **0.33.0** (1745–1747), `predecessors()`/`inter_diff()` in **0.37.0** (1180–1185), and removal of pre-0.30 legacy predecessor support in **0.42.0** (481–482). These are already applicable by 0.44.0, not unidentified future changes.

There is a documentation mismatch: the template table calls `operation()` an `Operation`, but the implementation maps the optional entry operation directly ([commit_templater.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/v0.44.0/cli/src/commit_templater.rs), `S00033`, 1480–1486), and the JSON test explicitly expects `"operation":null` (`S00019`, 269–275). `json(self)` is an available alternative to parsing display graphs, but that tested serialization contains commit and operation fields, **not explicit predecessor edges**; request predecessor IDs separately through templates if needed. Serialization backward compatibility is explicitly “not guaranteed” (`S00020`, 562–570). No stable cross-version adapter API is implied.

**Imported-history qualification.** The v0.44.0 clone fetch path (`S00006`, 384–388) explicitly sets `record_synthetic_predecessors: false`, with a comment about the potentially large number of new commits. The changelog reports synthetic history from preserved remote change IDs during `git fetch` starting in 0.42.0 (`S00009`, 495–497). These passages do not establish that a fresh clone recreates the producer's original evolution/operation history. Retain provenance and missing-history distinctions when importing repositories.
